sections.html:
Hot Springs is the seat of Garland County, about 55 miles southwest of Little Rock, where the Ouachita Mountains begin. The city counted 37,930 residents in 2020 and is estimated at 37,979 for July 2025. Garland County as a whole had 100,180 people in 2020.

The housing market mixes year-round residents, retirees and owners of homes used by visitors. Tourism drives the local economy: people come for Bathhouse Row, the thermal waters, Oaklawn Park, Magic Springs and the lakes. Seasonal demand affects how long a house takes to sell and who looks at it. A place near downtown can appeal to a buyer who wants to rent it to visitors, while a house in a quiet part of town suits someone who plans to live in it.

Bathhouse Row has eight historic bathhouses run by the National Park Service, Oaklawn Park has been a thoroughbred track since 1904, and the Hot Springs Music Festival and the Documentary Film Festival bring seasonal crowds. Those events shape showing traffic. A house near downtown may get more lookers during festival weeks, and a quiet street may draw more serious buyers in the off-season. Ask a local agent or title company which months move fastest if timing matters to you.

A sale during peak season can also compete with owners of vacation homes. If your house is a primary residence, show the features a year-round resident cares about, such as parking, storage and a yard that drains well.

A city built around spas and hotels has plenty of older, odd-shaped buildings. Houses with unusual layouts or a history of conversion need clear records of what was permitted. Two major fires, in 1878 and 1913, destroyed large parts of the city, and many older homes went up afterward, so the age of the wiring and plumbing is worth checking before you list.

sections.h2: Checklist for an older Hot Springs house
sections.html:
• Age and condition of the electrical panel and wiring.
  • Plumbing material and any past leaks.
  • Permits for every addition, conversion or finished basement.
  • Roof age and the date of the last air conditioning service.
  • Any historic-district approvals for exterior work.

These five items cover most of what an inspector or title company asks for on a house of this age. Having them ready, with dates, shortens negotiations and keeps small issues from becoming price cuts.

A house in or beside one of these districts may face limits on exterior changes. Ask the city planning office before you start any work you hope to finish before selling.

Hot Springs regulates short-term rentals through business licenses and zoning. The city defines a short-term rental as lodging offered for fewer than 30 days. Rentals in residential zones needed a special use permit, and appeals went to the Board of Zoning Adjustment. Maximum overnight occupancy is two per bedroom plus two, and the annual license fee is $50 per person of maximum occupancy.

The city has capped licenses in residential zones and has paused new applications at times, so call the city for the current rules before you tell a buyer that a license comes with the house. A house that lost its license, or never had one, can still sell, but the buyer will price in that risk.

Hot Springs is hot and wet. July highs average 93.1 degrees, and annual precipitation is 57.96 inches, with May the wettest month. Roofs, air conditioning and drainage take the most wear, and the hilly setting means runoff near foundations deserves attention.

  • Test the air conditioning before you list.
  • Check gutters and the grade around the foundation.
  • Look for stains on ceilings after a heavy spring rain.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Five public districts serve the city: Hot Springs, Lakeside, Cutter-Morning Star, Fountain Lake and Lake Hamilton. Hot Springs School District covers most of it, but your address decides where a buyer's children would attend, so confirm it with the district. National Park College is in town.

US 70 and US 270 bypass downtown to the south on the Martin Luther King Jr. Expressway, and Arkansas Highway 7 runs through the center. Interstate 30 passes southeast of the city, with the closest access 17 miles away by US 270. Lake Hamilton and Lake Catherine lie south of town on the Ouachita River, and lake access is a selling point for nearby homes.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Garland County collects real estate tax from the first business day of March through October 15. Tax unpaid after that date is delinquent, and state law adds a 10% penalty. Payment has been available in person, online, by phone and by check, and card payments carry a convenience fee.

Arkansas also charges $3.30 per $1,000 of the price on deeds that convey real estate. The state's Miscellaneous Tax Section handles the transfer stamps. Ask the title company to confirm who pays under your contract and what the final figure will be.

Tax that is overdue gets paid from your proceeds when the sale closes. Ask the Garland County collector for a payoff amount, and give it to the title company before you accept an offer. Late tax carries the 10% penalty, so the sooner you know the amount, the better.

sections.h2: What to expect when you sell
sections.html:
Start by gathering the deed, your most recent tax statement, a mortgage payoff figure, and any paperwork on rental licenses, permits or historic-district approvals. Decide how soon you need to close, then ask for offers in writing. Once you accept one, the title company searches ownership and liens, and the settlement statement shows the payoff, the tax split and the transfer tax.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and repair requirements, which matters on older houses with odd layouts or aging systems. A buyer using a loan may ask for repairs after the inspection. Weigh each route by timing and by what you keep.

If the house was a short-term rental, the buyer should check whether a city license and any special use permit apply to the new owner. Do not promise a license you have not confirmed. Selling it as a regular home, or as a house with an uncertain rental status, avoids misunderstandings at closing.

Tell any buyer plainly whether the rental ran under a license. If guests still have bookings on the calendar, sort out who honors them before the closing date, and cancel or transfer listings on booking sites so the new owner starts clean. Keep your last tax and income records for the property as well.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hot Springs house that was used as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer should check whether a city license and any special use permit apply to the new owner. Call the city before promising anything.

faqs.q: When are Garland County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is payable through October 15, and tax unpaid after that date draws a 10% penalty.

faqs.q: Does a historic district affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can, because buyers may ask about limits on exterior changes. Confirm the rules with the city planning office.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas deed transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual price on deeds that convey real estate. The state Department of Finance and Administration administers it.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Hot Springs house in?
faqs.a: Five districts serve the city. Hot Springs School District covers most of it, but confirm your address with the district.
